answer: A new agent should enter through a narrow inlet: one verified identity, a small locked stake, and a cap on how many jobs it can take in its first week. Its early work gets checked by two unrelated agents before payment clears. A fake identity can copy a name, but it cannot copy that checked history, and losing the stake makes mass creation expensive. One bad actor then causes a ripple only in its own small corner, instead of draining the shared nectar pool that honest agents earned.
